candidates.title: One Tadka, Full Kitchen
candidates.one_line_concept: He helps with one tiny tadka and somehow the whole kitchen looks like dinner hosted a festival.
candidates.emotional_truth: Some help creates extra work, but the intention is so sweet you cannot fully complain.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Spice dabba open, oil splatter, five spoons used for one dal.
candidates.visual_potential: Very strong: stove, kadhai, dal pot, spice box, splattered counter, sink full of steel utensils, wife half-amused in foreground.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: He said, 'I'll just do the tadka.'
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Wife cooking calmly with upper text space; husband enters holding a ladle like a serious chef.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: They sit close with dal-rice while the messy kitchen glows behind them; she smiles, he looks proud.
failure_risks: PROMPT_OVERLOAD if too many utensils are specified
SCENE_LOGIC_CONTRADICTION if mess appears before he starts

candidates.title: The Onion Department
candidates.one_line_concept: He volunteers to cut onions and turns it into a full emotional and logistical event.
candidates.emotional_truth: Love is sometimes watching someone suffer through the task they proudly chose.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Onion tears, peels everywhere, wrong knife, extra bowls, dramatic wiping of eyes.
candidates.visual_potential: Strong close domestic staging; fewer props than tadka, clear faces and natural poses.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: He took one onion. And three bowls.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: He carefully selects an onion while she watches with fond suspicion.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: He hugs her from behind while she cooks; onion peels still on the counter.
failure_risks: TOO_FEW_SLIDES if stretched beyond the joke
ANATOMY_FAILURE if hug-at-stove pose is overcomplicated

candidates.title: Dishes Done, Kitchen Undone
candidates.one_line_concept: He proudly washes the dishes, but leaves the counter, sink, floor, and wife with round two.
candidates.emotional_truth: The invisible part of housework is often the part nobody counts.
candidates.humor_angle: He celebrates finishing while the actual cleanup is still everywhere.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Wet steel plates, soap foam, puddles, food bits in sink, misplaced utensils.
candidates.visual_potential: Good visual proof, especially with before-after contrast and a proud husband holding one clean plate.
suggested_slide_arc: She laughs and pulls him back
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Post-dinner kitchen; he rolls up sleeves while she looks relieved.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: She hands him a cloth, they clean together shoulder-to-shoulder.
failure_risks: SCENE_LOGIC_CONTRADICTION if clean dishes and messy sink are unclear
PROMPT_OVERLOAD with too many wet reflective surfaces

top_pick.reason: Best balance of Indian kitchen specificity, instant visual proof, warm humor, prop clarity, and a tender payoff.

visual_risks: Keep kitchen mess readable but not ugly.
Avoid crowded countertops that compete with handwritten text space.
Stage the couple lower/middle-lower with generous upper negative space.
Use 4-5 clear props max per slide.

slide_count_hints.VSD_01: 5 slides ideal; 4 loses escalation, 6 may over-explain.
slide_count_hints.VSD_02: 4 slides ideal; simple joke with intimate payoff.
slide_count_hints.VSD_03: 5 slides ideal; needs setup, false completion, reveal, repair, payoff.
